Cyber Manhunt Demo Declaration
We are very glad you decided to try the trailer of Cyber Manhunt. Before start, please let us give some explanations about the demo and the game. We wish it can help you understand this game better.

Therefore, we decided to develop a game related to the theme of "Hacker", "Cyber Manhunt" and "Privacy Data Breaches", allowing players to be a hacker and apply social engineering technique on the target person, find out their privacy and secrets. Manipulate the destiny of the target person above him/her like a "god" and witness their endings. We wish through this process, players could consider the incident in-depth and make their judgments. Maybe one day, players experience similar incidents in reality. Please make the decision with kindness and humanity.

The name of the game is called "Cyber Manhunt" for now, because we feel that such a word not only summarize the theme of the game but also leave a space that players can imagine. Of course, if there is a better or more appropriate name, we will consider replacing it.

Yesterday, police accidentally found the charred body of a man in the back hills of . Due to the severity of the damage to the body, it is impossible to discern its identity, but police suspect the body to be that of the recently missing Austin Hill. The body has been rushed to a forensic center for identification, and Austin's family has been notified to help with identification. Police said they would release specific information to the public as soon as possible.

According to a source, the coroner performed an autopsy on the body and tentatively confirmed that the body died between 6 p.m. and 10 p.m. on Nov. 3rd, with the cause of death being a severe blow to the back of the head. And police has confirmed the body to be Austin Hill and that the body was hidden away after being severely burned in a fire. Rather coincidentally there was a fire at on the night of the 3rd, and a student named Jim reported the fire. Police have now shifted their attention to this fire, and those involved are being investigated.

Although the company rejected the proposal for a self-aware artificial intelligence, earlier in a series of experiments, I believe I have found the "key" and am only one step away from success. Artificial intelligence evolves at a rate that obeys Moore's Law - doubling performance every 18 months, while the rate of human evolution is 20 years per generation. If my theoretical experiment in artificial intelligence succeeds, it will be a discovery big enough to shake the entire academic world, no, it will be an evolution. Nothing will stop me.
The new experiment sample (experiment no. 73511178) passed the Turing test perfectly and ended up having high level of perception, but there were problems with the key point of self-awareness. The experiment sample wouldn't doubt its own existence. It was after all still a machine.
Exactly what went wrong is not yet known for certain. Perhaps the experiment was headed in the wrong direction, but fortunately I had a backup plan ready.
The volunteer Van was involved in another experimental project (experiment no. -003), in which I simulated the conscious behavior of his brain in the hope that this would create a new self-aware artificial intelligence.

During the investigation, the system successfully detected the hack set up by the culprit to prevent us from tracking him down. The system was able to identify the mastermind behind it by analyzing hierarchical relationships, and successfully hacked into his server to destroy the missing data to save the company's losses. This is exactly the kind of performance that I mentioned before, and it is certain to have a positive impact on the company's next business development.
The mysterious man behind this calls himself "Van", and we're still unable to find anything about him in our database. His target this time was our important experimental data, thus we must increase security. I suggest conducting an in-depth investigation into this person to prevent the recurrence of similar incidents in the future.
Report concluded.
